scope: Actual saved full17 trajectory geometric nearness and restricted low-node winding; no force/contact-causality inference, no runtime/config changes
sample_definition: Every cloth vertex, unique edge midpoint and face centroid, searched against exact current teddy boundary triangles. Only samples in teddy AABB expanded by20 mm evaluated; first-near times are first observed sampled proximity, not exact continuous contact onset.
group_note: Panel vertex/edge masks include shared U seams; face centroids use explicit source front/back triangle labels. Handle masks include shared sewn roots.

limitations: 50ms saved geometry can miss earlier contact between frames; no statement that a region had zero earlier contact follows from this discrete sampling.
Distances are upper bounds on continuous surface minimum from sampled cloth points, not per-pair forces.
Signed panel normals near edges/folds can be ambiguous; orientation alone cannot prove contact-side history.
Restricted winding uses only queries at least2 mm below every rim vertex; two high caps agree there. No cap-independence claim for the much larger portion above the lowest rim.
Most teddy nodes still lie above the lowest rim; the low-node exterior result does not establish impossibility of a subsequent physical centering/insertion motion.

body_and_rim.bear_rest_region_interpretation: Unheld-side outer arm, local rest approximately[-.116,-.025,.042] m

interpretation: Observed nearness begins against the held front handle during X transport, followed during lowering by the right upper bag-mouth/seam corner and upper panel regions. The first body event is not a free central drop into an open cavity.

Panel-interior nearest pairs, excluding triangle-edge ambiguities, lie on the original outward side in all reviewed near frames. Restricted low-region winding independently finds all sufficiently low teddy nodes outside the body. Together these support exterior-side engagement during entry, beyond merely being above the rim.

This evidence does not establish interpenetration: original native gates passed this prefix, and sampled nearness is not contact force. It also does not prove the future center-and-insert motion will fail; the bag mouth may rearrange around the teddy under contact.
Negative-X centering addresses the measured exterior-side offset geometrically, but passing a convex contact-envelope COM gate does not demonstrate that the actual mouth has enveloped the teddy.

For a later failure/success review, compare the same restricted low-node winding and local panel-side signals after actual centering and throughout insertion; only final whole-teddy containment plus actual release/stability can establish completion.
